_comment: New Jersey QAP, N.J.A.C. 5:80-33, adopted February 2, 2026 (58 N.J.R. 991(a)). A regulation, cited by subsection. Page numbers are PDF page indices and match the printed page numbers. Scoring is 33.14 to 33.19, PDF pp.46-62. THREE CYCLES, which a project cannot enter simultaneously (33.3): Family (33.15), Age-Friendly Senior (33.16) and Supportive Housing (33.17). The Senior and Supportive Housing scales are defined as the Family scale minus named categories plus their own. Coded as a core track of the categories every cycle uses, plus one add-on track per cycle, so each cycle's maximum is core + its add-on. Only 33.15(a)21 had to be recorded twice, because it is in the Family and Senior scales but not the Supportive Housing one. NO MAXIMUM IS STATED anywhere, yet 33.14(a) sets the floor as 'a minimum of 65 percent of the maximum score'. Hand-summed before loading: core 75 (20+2+5+5+2+6+4+2+6+3+4+1+3+3+8+1); family add-on 22 (5+6+5+3+3), so Family = 97; senior add-on 13 (3+1+9), so Senior = 88; supportive add-on 23 (2+1+5+2+2+2+2+2+5), so Supportive Housing = 98. The loader matched all four. These maxima include the '(a)25 bonus point', which the scale lists as an ordinary category. TUM location changes the ceiling: a TUM project can earn 15 rather than 20 under (a)1 and 2 rather than 3 under (a)14iv-v, so a Family project in a TUM tops out at 91. Eight deduction categories run from -1 per cured defect (no maximum) to -15, and four of them also bar the application from every set-aside. Thresholds are in NJ_thresholds.json.

track_totals.note: Core categories common to all three cycles: 75, hand-summed and matched. Not a total any project faces on its own; add the cycle's track. No maximum score is stated in the regulation, although 33.14(a) sets eligibility at '65 percent of the maximum score'.
Family Cycle add-on: 22, for a Family Cycle maximum of 97 (91 inside a TUM). 65% of 97 is 63.05. The Family Cycle receives not less than 50% of competitive credits.
Age-Friendly Senior Cycle add-on: 13, for a Senior Cycle maximum of 88. 33.16(a) excludes the Family categories (a)3, (a)5, (a)14ii and (a)14iii.

Supportive Housing Cycle add-on: 23, for a Supportive Housing maximum of 98. 33.17(a) excludes (a)3, (a)5 and (a)21 and replaces (a)14ii and iii, 'for a maximum of seven points available pursuant to N.J.A.C. 5:80-33.15(a)14'; the shared 14i (1) and 14iv-v (3) plus the replacements (2 + 1) make exactly that seven.

criteria.native_category: Point system for the Family Cycle

Inside a TUM, compliance period extended 15 years
Single-family and duplex housing converting to tenant ownership

criteria.note: The largest category in every cycle. The same 15-year extension is worth 20 outside a TUM and 15 inside one, so location, not commitment, sets the value. The Mixed-Income and Emerging Developer set-asides (33.4(a)1 and 3) require the maximum here.

15-year fixed-rate abatement above 6.28%

criteria.note: Projects without an abatement score nothing and must instead capitalize two years of taxes in escrow and carry a 1.20 debt coverage ratio with at least $3,000 per unit core operating expenses. Nonprofit tax-exempt status does not count as an abatement.

50% or more but less than 100%

At least 15% but less than 20%

criteria.note: Two ladders, ownership and construction spending, each an internal choice of one option, under a combined 5-point maximum. The ownership route requires the M/WBE to earn at least its ownership share of paid and deferred developer fee and to stay in the ownership entity through the compliance period.

criteria.native_category: Point system for the Family Cycle
criteria.heading: Proximity to positive land uses
criteria.quote: 11. Applications may receive up to a maximum of six points for the following (to be eligible for

tiers.tier_label: Within one-half mile of each of eight priority uses (grocery, hospital/clinic, school, senior center, day care, family success center, one-stop career center, community mental health center), per use
Within three miles (Family) or one mile (Senior and Supportive Housing) of any of twenty listed uses, per use

criteria.note: Capped at 6. The per-use values are those stated; the tier rows here are the two rates, not an enumeration of all twenty uses. Several uses are restricted by cycle (grocery non-senior unless transport is provided, school non-senior, mental health center Supportive Housing only). Multiple instances of one category do not add. The Mixed-Income and Emerging Developer set-asides require the maximum here. The regulation's own worked example (p.53) gives a project near a school, a grocery store and an oil refinery one point, netting the refinery's deduction under (a)11ii against the positive points.
